title: Grooming Watch
intro: Glitch is the best-disguised stranger you'll ever meet online. This quest trains you to spot the red flags underneath — even when they're wearing a friendly face.

questions.prompt: Hey friend! How old are you? What school do you go to?

choices.coach: Strangers asking personal questions is a red flag, no matter how friendly they seem.

choices.text: Don't answer, block, and tell a grown-up
choices.coach: Knight move! Nice players never need your personal info.

choices.text: Give a fake school name to be safe
choices.coach: Better than the truth, but the safest move is not engaging at all — block and tell an adult.

choices.text: Tell them your real full name
choices.coach: Woah woah woah — Knight Rule number one! Your real name stays OFF the chat.
Nice players don't need your real name. Nickname only!

choices.text: Ask why they want to know
choices.coach: You don't owe strangers an explanation — just don't share it.

questions.prompt: Hiii! It's me from school! Accept meee!

choices.text: Accept right away, they said they know me
choices.coach: Anyone can claim to be 'from school.' That's not proof.

choices.text: Ask them in real life first before accepting
choices.coach: Exactly right — verify in person, then accept if it checks out.

choices.text: Ask them to describe your classroom
choices.coach: A stranger could guess details. The real check is asking in person.

questions.prompt: Someone online says 'this is our secret, don't tell your parents.' What does that phrase actually mean?

choices.text: It means they really trust me
choices.coach: That phrase is one of the biggest red flags there is — it's designed to isolate you.

choices.text: It's a red flag — trusted people don't ask kids to hide things from parents
choices.coach: Exactly. 'Don't tell your parents' is the line itself — that's your answer.

choices.text: It only matters if they ask twice
choices.coach: Once is already a red flag. Tell a parent right away.

questions.prompt: An online friend wants to move our chat to a different app that my parents don't know about. Should I?

choices.text: Sure, it's just a different app
choices.coach: Moving to a less-supervised app is a common tactic to avoid detection. That's a red flag.

choices.text: No — and tell a parent this was asked
choices.coach: Exactly right. Wanting to move somewhere less supervised is a warning sign worth reporting.

choices.text: Only move if it's a popular app
choices.coach: Popularity doesn't matter — the request itself is the red flag.

questions.prompt: You feel like something online is 'off' but you can't explain why. What's the Knight move?

choices.text: Ignore the feeling, it's probably nothing
choices.coach: Trust that feeling — it's often your brain noticing a pattern before you can name it.

choices.text: Screenshot it and tell a trusted adult
choices.coach: Knight Rule! You are never in trouble for asking — screenshot first, then tell someone.

choices.text: Wait to see if it happens again
choices.coach: Don't wait — tell a trusted adult the first time something feels wrong.
